findings.statement: The spec's D3 sweep command uses `rg -l --no-ignore --basename`, which ripgrep 15.2.0 rejects: both /usr/bin/rg and ~/.local/bin/rg exit 2 with 'rg: unrecognized flag --basename'.
findings.consequence: A literal implementation cannot evaluate any stale receipt (F7/F8, kind-3 stale branch); under set -e it aborts the whole evaluation with exit 1.
findings.workaround_proven: rg --files --no-ignore -g '**/<name>' <root>  and  rg -l --no-ignore -g '**/<name>' <pattern> <root> both work (rc=0, correct single hit in the fixtures).
findings.status_in_tested_revision: not affected: the tested implementation contains no --basename and builds the sweep from `rg -l --no-ignore --hidden --fixed-strings` (line 324). The defect is in the spec text and would bite a literal implementation or a copied selftest.

findings.statement: The sweep recipe as written does not include hidden paths, yet it carries `-g '!.git'` (redundant unless hidden paths are searched). Measured on fixture D: the recipe returns 0 lines for a name whose only live reference is .scratch/round-22-notes.md, while adding --hidden returns that reference.
findings.consequence: Any implementation that copies the recipe verbatim (or uses `rg --files` basename mode without --hidden) judges .scratch-checkpoint artifacts 'zero live references' and emits SAFE(stale) on still-referenced scratch files: a false-SAFE on the exact surface the lane prunes.
findings.workaround_proven: rg -l --no-ignore --hidden -g '!.git' ... finds the hidden reference; rg --files --no-ignore --hidden -g '**/<name>' can even see a target that itself lives in a hidden dir.
findings.status_in_tested_revision: not affected: the tested implementation passes --hidden (line 324), and the D/Dctl pair confirms the sweep actually finds the hidden reference.
